related_questions.question: What should you do if you test positive for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, the first step is to contact your healthcare provider to discuss your situation and potential treatment options, especially if you have underlying health conditions or experience severe symptoms. You should also isolate yourself at home, rest, stay hydrated, and manage symptoms with over-the-counter medications. Monitor your symptoms and report any worsening to your healthcare provider. If you experience severe symptoms like difficulty breathing or chest pain, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911.
snippet_highlighted_words: contact your healthcare provider to discuss your situation and potential treatment options

list.title: Contact your healthcare provider:
list.snippet: Inform them of your positive test result and discuss your symptoms and health history.

list.title: Consider early treatment:
list.snippet: Depending on your risk factors and symptoms, your doctor might recommend specific treatments, like antiviral medications, that are most effective when started early.
Stay home: Isolate yourself from others to prevent further spread of the virus.
Get plenty of rest: Allow your body to recover by resting and minimizing physical activity.
Stay hydrated: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, which is important for recovery.

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:
list.snippet: Use medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen to manage fever, aches, and pains.

list.title: Monitor your symptoms:
list.snippet: Pay close attention to your symptoms and report any worsening to your healthcare provider.

text_blocks.snippet: 4. Seek Immediate Medical Care for Severe Symptoms:

list.title: Call 911:
list.snippet: If you experience severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, or new confusion, call emergency services immediately.

list.title: Notify emergency responders:
list.snippet: Inform them that you have COVID-19 and are experiencing emergency warning signs.

list.snippet: Inform your doctor or healthcare provider about your positive test result.
They can assess your specific situation (age, underlying health conditions, etc.) and recommend the best course of action.
Early treatment, when appropriate, can help reduce the risk of severe illness, according to the CDC.
Rest: Get plenty of sleep and avoid overexertion.
Stay Hydrated: Drink lots of fluids to prevent dehydration.
Manage Symptoms: Over-the-counter medications can help alleviate symptoms like fever, aches, and cough.
Monitor Symptoms: Keep track of your symptoms and any changes, and report worsening symptoms to your healthcare provider.
Difficulty breathing .
Persistent pain or pressure in the chest .
New confusion .
If any other symptoms worsen .
Contact emergency services (911) and inform them about your COVID-19 status and the emergency warning signs you are experiencing, according to the American Lung Association.
Isolate: Stay away from others to prevent spreading the virus.
Follow isolation guidelines: Follow your healthcare provider's or local health department's recommendations for isolation.
Masks and Ventilation: If you need to be around others, wear a high-quality mask and ensure good ventilation.
